item.title: Hyperon--nucleon interactions at BESIII
item.description: arXiv:2610.20756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperon--nucleon interactions provide essential information on the strange sector of baryon--baryon forces, with implications for hypernuclei, dense baryonic matter, and non-perturbative QCD. Direct experimental information, however, remains scarce because hyperons are short lived and intense conventional hyperon beams are difficult to produce. At BESIII, hyperons and antihyperons produced in charmonium decays can instead be used as incident particles, while the detector material serves as an effective fixed target. This approach has enabled a new program of hyperon--nucleon studies at an $e^+e^-$ collider. Representative results include the first study of $\Xi^{0}n\to\Xi^-p$ using $\Xi^0$--nucleus scattering, measurements of elastic $\Lambda p\to\Lambda p$ and $\bar{\Lambda}p\to\bar{\Lambda}p$ scattering, and recent observations of $\bar{\Lambda}p$ annihilation into multi-meson final states. These measurements demonstrate that BESIII can operate as an effective hyperon--nucleon scattering facility and provide new experimental constraints on the poorly explored strange sector of baryon--baryon interactions.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Fei Shen

item.title: First Observation of the Radiative Decay $D^0 \to \gamma\omega$
item.description: arXiv:2610.21982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the first observation of the radiative charm decay $D^0 \to \gamma \omega$ with a significance of $6.0\sigma$. The analysis uses 20.3\,$\rm{fb}^{-1}$ of $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at a center-of-mass energy of 3.773\,GeV, and employs a deep learning strategy based on the Particle Transformer architecture. The absolute branching fraction of $\mathcal{B}(D^0\to\gamma\omega)=(2.12\pm 0.40_{\rm stat}\pm 0.25_{\rm syst})\times 10^{-5}$ confirms the dominance of long-distance hadronic dynamics in radiative charm decays and provides a valuable benchmark for testing non-perturbative QCD calculations of $D \to \gamma V$ transitions.

item.title: Machine-learning-based neutrino-event generation constrained by experimental measurements
item.description: arXiv:2610.20870v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a generative surrogate for charged-current \(\nu_\mu\)-nucleus scattering that can be calibrated to measured differential cross sections without event-level experimental samples. Starting from a theoretical interaction model, we fine-tune the surrogate to a MicroBooNE measurement and show that this also improves the description of observables not used in the fit. The calibrated model can also be applied to measurements from different neutrino fluxes without retuning, while retaining event-level predictions of outgoing-muon kinematics. Our results show that experimental cross sections can directly constrain generative event models while preserving their applicability across different observables and beam configurations.
item.dc:creator: Jose Luis Bonilla, Krzysztof M. Graczyk, Rwik Dharmapal Banerjee, Beata E. Kowal, Hemant Prasad, Jan T. Sobczyk

item.title: The Sill distribution for all partial waves
item.description: arXiv:2610.20975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In high-energy physics, short-lived resonances appearing in scattering processes are described by energy-dependent spectral functions. The relativistic Breit--Wigner distribution (rBW), obtained as a relativistic extension of the standard Breit--Wigner form, is commonly employed owing to its simplicity. However, when the lower-energy threshold lies sufficiently close to the resonance peak, sizable deviations from the rBW line shape are expected. The Sill distribution provides a simple way to incorporate the physical threshold while preserving exact normalization, but in its original formulation it is inherently restricted to $s$-wave decays. Here, we extend the Sill distribution to arbitrary partial waves. The correct $\ell$-wave threshold behaviour is implemented while exact normalization is retained through a simple modification of the mass term of the propagator. As a benchmark, the $p$-wave Sill provides a very good description of the $\Delta(1232)^{++}$ line shape up to 1.35 GeV and simultaneously reproduces its on-shell mass and width and its complex pole position, in agreement with independent determinations compiled by the PDG.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof Kyzio{\l}, Francesco Giacosa

item.title: Disentangling geometry & growth in cosmic neutrino mass constraints: a more physical split and diagnostic
item.description:
arXiv:2610.20977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent cosmological data hint at a neutrino mass sum below the minimum value allowed by the neutrino mass oscillation experiments, with a preference for the opposite of massive neutrinos ("negative" neutrino masses). Since massive neutrinos impact the expansion history of the Universe, which in turn modifies the growth of structure, we ask whether such a preference originates from the observed geometry or structure growth, and whether the two agree. In this paper, we introduce a more physical split of $\sum m_
u$ into parameters $\sum m_
u^{geo}$ and $\sum m_
u^{growth}$ based on their physical effects, with extension to negative values. We split the expansion rate at the Boltzmann-code level: $\sum m_
u^{geo}$ sets $H(z)$ for distance computation, and $\sum m_
u^{growth}$ sets $H(z)$ for perturbation evolution. Combining Planck primary CMB, Planck+ACT+SPT CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, we find similar sensitivity and "negative" preference from geometry and growth with $\sum m_
u^{geo} = -0.07\pm0.10$ eV (68% C.L.) and $\sum m_
u^{growth} = -0.13^{+0.10}_{-0.12}$ eV (68% C.L.). The difference of the two is a null test of the $\Lambda$CDM model, passed by current data at $0.4\sigma$ level. Forecasts on Advanced SO CMB and DESI DR3 BAO show that $0.058$ eV would be rejected at $3.0\sigma$ from the geometry channel alone, if the negative mean of $\sum m_
u^{geo} = -0.07$ eV persists. The two channels can also provide a powerful new diagnostic between possible origins of the neutrino mass tension. With future CMB and BAO data, our Fisher forecasts show that an incorrect dark energy model displaces $\sum m_
u^{geo}$ from $0.058$ eV by $3.1$-$4.2\sigma$ and $\sum m_
u^{growth}$ by $1.1$-$1.3\sigma$, while an underestimated reionization optical depth reverses the pattern, $2.7$-$3.6\sigma$ in $\sum m_
u^{growth}$ against at most $0.23\sigma$ in $\sum m_
u^{geo}$. (Abridged)
item.dc:creator: Fei Ge, Frank J. Qu, Hanyue Wang, Emmanuel Schaan, W. L. Kimmy Wu, Alexander Friedland

item.title: Testing the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the LZ event with heavy-element experiments
item.description: arXiv:2610.21041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the recent 248 keV event observed by LZ and identify different experiments that could test it. Details of the underlying model and the ability of complementary experiments to test it depend significantly on the high-velocity tail of the dark matter distribution. We consider several example velocity distributions motivated by the impact of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) in order to map out the effects of this dependence. For example, we illustrate the type of high-velocity tail that would make the thermal Higgsino viable despite stringent constraints from solar neutrinos: Reducing the flux of the tail relative to simulation results improves the Higgsino fit, while extending the tail to higher velocities at fluxes below current simulation resolution evades the solar neutrino bound. This motivates more detailed simulations at higher resolution to understand the tail better. Even if xenon experiments confirm the signal event, complementary experiments are still required to test whether the underlying model is inelastic dark matter and to break degeneracies in the measurement of dark matter parameters such as mass and mass splitting. Heavy-element paleodetectors could cover most of the parameter space relevant to the LZ event. Their use of different elements could determine the dark matter mass and splitting, while their unique sensitivity to the history of the dark matter distribution could test the signal's LMC origin. Luminous detection in large neutrino detectors with heavy-element supplements could directly test the inelastic nature of the signal and measure the mass splitting, while its sensitivity to the radiative decay rate could provide strong evidence for the Higgsino interpretation.
item.dc:creator: Peter W. Graham, Juan P. Luengas, Harikrishnan Ramani, Samuel S. Y. Wong

item.title: Dark Matter Particle Explorer: Ten-Year On-Orbit Performance and Scientific Outcomes
item.description: arXiv:2610.21168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Dark Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE, also known as ``Wukong'') is the first scientific space mission within the framework of the Strategic Pioneer Program on Space Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The main scientific objectives of DAMPE include indirect detection of dark matter, cosmic-ray physics, and high energy gamma-ray astronomy. Thanks to its large geometrical factor and thick imaging calorimeter, DAMPE could effectively detect cosmic-ray electrons (including positrons) and gamma-rays up to 10~TeV, and nuclei up to PeV. Since launched on 17 December 2015 into a Sun-synchronous orbit, DAMPE has been smoothly operating on orbit for more than ten years. Here we present an overview of instrument, on-orbit status, and highlight scientific results of DAMPE, including the measurements of the all-electron energy spectrum and the spectra of protons and other nuclei, and high energy gamma-ray line search.
item.dc:creator: Jian-Hua Guo, Chuan Yue, Yun-Long Zhang, Yi-Zhong Fan, Jin Chang

item.title: Revisiting $B_c^{(*)}$ production in $Z$-boson decays at NLO in QCD
item.description: arXiv:2610.21485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study $B_c^{(*)}$ production in $Z$-boson decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD within the color-singlet nonrelativistic QCD framework. The analysis covers both the $1S$ and $2S$ pseudoscalar and vector states, extending the phenomenological study to radially excited $B_c$ mesons. We calculate direct production widths and energy-fraction and invariant-mass distributions, including both charm- and bottom-quark production topologies. For the central inputs and $\mu_R=2m_b$, the $K$ factors are $1.52$ for $B_c$ and $1.33$ for $B_c^*$. We examine uncertainties from the renormalization scale, heavy-quark masses, and wave functions at the origin, and apply the principle of maximum conformality to fix the renormalization scale from the $\beta_0$-dependent NLO contribution. The NLO corrections enhance the small- and intermediate-energy-fraction regions and modify the invariant-mass spectra. We discuss these features in relation to heavy-quark fragmentation. The results provide production-rate and kinematic inputs for studies of ground-state and radially excited $B_c$ mesons at high-statistics $Z$ factories.
item.dc:creator: Qi-Wei Ke, Lei Guo, Jun Zeng, Xu-Chang Zheng

item.title: Identification of ultra-high-energy neutrinos in vertical air showers with surface detectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.21495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the potential of surface detector arrays to identify ultra-high-energy neutrinos using vertical air showers with zenith angle $\theta \leq 60^\circ$, a region largely unexplored in current searches. The method exploits the enhanced electromagnetic component at ground level arising from energetic leptons produced in neutrino interactions. Using detailed air-shower and detector simulations, we show that observables sensitive to the electromagnetic and muonic content provide genuine discrimination between neutrino-induced and hadron-induced showers. This is demonstrated both with idealized shower quantities and with realistic detector-level signals based on water-Cherenkov and scintillator detectors. The corresponding neutrino identification efficiency is used to derive the effective mass and, primarily, the effective area of the array under background-rejection requirements appropriate to targeted multi-messenger searches. Although not competitive with inclined-shower searches under the stringent background rejection factors required for diffuse-flux analyses, this approach establishes the feasibility of a vertical detection channel, extending the field of view of surface arrays and providing a complementary tool for multi-messenger observations of transient sources.
item.dc:creator: Jaime Alvarez-Mu\~niz, Ruben Concei\c{c}\~ao, Pedro J. Costa, David Dias, M\'ario Pimenta

item.title: Radiative transitions of hybrid mesons
item.description: arXiv:2610.22088v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radiative transitions of hybrid mesons probe nonperturbative gluodynamics, particularly the interplay between quark spin and gluonic excitations, and are of direct relevance to the search for exotic hadrons at Jefferson Lab. We calculate these transitions across the lowest charmonium-hybrid multiplet in a constituent gluon model based on Coulomb-gauge QCD in the heavy quark expansion. The results for $Y\to\eta_c\gamma$ and $Y\to \chi_{c0}\gamma$ overlap the width obtained in quenched lattice computations, whereas $\eta_{c1}\to J/\psi\gamma$ is substantially below the corresponding lattice estimate.
item.dc:creator: Shahriyar Jafarzade, Eric S. Swanson

item.title: From Axion Detection to Dark Matter Astronomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.22105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A global haloscope network could turn an axion discovery into astronomy of dark matter substructure and transients. We combine interferometric phase, spatial coherence, and spectroscopy to study the formation and evolution of axion substructure through measurements of flow directions and velocity distributions. For tidal streams, a four-site forecast shows how longitudinal and transverse velocity dispersions can be measured jointly. Interpreted with dynamical and population models, these measurements could test axion production scenarios. Extensions to miniclusters, axion stars, and emitted bursts would broaden the astrophysical reach of laboratory detection.
item.dc:creator: Jae Hyeok Chang, Stefano Profumo

item.title: Gallium Anomaly and Solar Neutrinos
item.description: arXiv:2610.22219v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Gallium Anomaly is the disagreement between the measured capture rate of neutrinos by $^{71}$Ga and the rate theoretically expected from the electron capture decay of $^{71}$Ge. The experimental measurements were performed with intense artificial sources. In the present work we consider the sun as a neutrino source that can be calibrated via the fundamental, standard-model neutrino-electron elastic scattering reaction in terrestrial detectors. The result is found to be not anomalous, with good agreement between the measured value of $66.1\pm3.1$ SNU from SAGE and Gallex/GNO, and the total measured source strengths of solar sources, $67.5^{+1.4}_{-1.1}$ SNU. It may be concluded that neither the $^{71}$Ga charged-current cross section nor gallium experiment extraction and counting efficiencies account for the Gallium Anomaly.

item.title: Inclusive Search for Anomalous Single-Photon Production in MicroBooNE
item.description: arXiv:2502.06064v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an inclusive search for anomalous production of single-photon events from neutrino interactions in the MicroBooNE experiment. The search and its signal definition are motivated by the previous observation of a low-energy excess of electromagnetic shower events from the MiniBooNE experiment. We use the Wire-Cell reconstruction framework to select a sample of inclusive single-photon final-state interactions with a final efficiency and purity of 7.0% and 40.2%, respectively. We leverage simultaneous measurements of sidebands of charged current $\nu_{\mu}$ interactions and neutral current interactions producing $\pi^{0}$ mesons to constrain signal and background predictions and reduce uncertainties. We perform a blind analysis using a dataset collected from February 2016 to July 2018, corresponding to an exposure of $6.34\times10^{20}$ protons on target from the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB) at Fermilab. In the full signal region, we observe agreement between the data and the prediction, with a goodness-of-fit $p$-value of 0.11. We then isolate a sub-sample of these events containing no visible protons, and observe $93\pm22\text{(stat.)}\pm35\text{(syst.)}$ data events above prediction, corresponding to just above $2\sigma$ local significance, concentrated at shower energies below 600 MeV.

item.title: A Novel Approach to Short Baseline Oscillation Searches Using Neutrino Tagging with nuSCOPE
item.description:
arXiv:2606.14263v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the first study of short-baseline neutrino oscillation searches using a tagged neutrino beamline, taking the proposed nuSCOPE facility at CERN as a benchmark. In this Letter we demonstrate that tagged neutrino beams, where the neutrino flavor, energy, and propagation distance are determined with exceptional event-by-event precision, provide a new experimental approach to search for non-standard neutrino oscillations. We evaluate the sensitivity to sterile-neutrino-induced oscillations in the $
u_\mu$ disappearance, $
u_\mu ightarrow 
u_e$ appearance, and $
u_e$ disappearance channels, demonstrating the ability to probe multiple flavor transitions and both appearance and disappearance modes within a single experiment. Our results show that tagged beams enable sensitivity improvements to mass-squared splittings spanning several orders of magnitude while substantially reducing the dependence on neutrino flux predictions that limits conventional searches. We find that nuSCOPE can probe a broad region of parameter space motivated by existing anomalies and extend coverage into previously unexplored territory, demonstrating the strong potential of tagged neutrino beams for precision oscillation physics.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Blanchet, C\'esar Jes\'us-Valls, Animesh Chatterjee, Stephen Dolan, Pierre Granger, Laura Munteanu

item.title: Construction and Performance of the sMDT Precision Muon Tracking Chambers for ATLAS at the HL-LHC
item.description: arXiv:2609.01546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In order to improve the muon trigger efficiency and the rate capability of the ATLAS muon detectors for operation at the high luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC), the Monitored Drift Tube (MDT) tracking chambers in the inner barrel layer of the ATLAS Muon Spectrometer will be replaced by small-diameter Muon Drift Tube (sMDT) chambers integrated with new thin-gap RPC trigger chambers. The sMDT chambers are in serial production since January 2021. This documentation provides insight into the drift tube production and every step performed in the chamber construction at the MPI Munich. The serial production involves a stringent quality control program to assure the reliability and high mechanical precision of the chambers. This program consists of tests of the individual drift tubes, measurements of the chamber geometry and proof of gas tightness. Final certification at the production site is provided using cosmic rays. The dedicated quality control database and monitoring Web interface that is used commonly for both production sites of the sMDT chambers is presented
item.dc:creator: D. A. Buchin, O. Kortner, H. Kroha, A. Reed, M. Rendel, P. Rieck, E. Voevodina, V. M. Walbrecht

item.title: Internal energy of the medium formed in pp collisions
item.description: arXiv:2509.14175v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we perform a thermostatistical analysis of the charged particles produced in minimum bias pp collisions across different energies available at the LHC-CERN reported by the ALICE Collaboration. To this end, we adopted the normalized $\pT$ spectrum as the probability density function governing the $\pT$ microstates of the produced hadrons, from which we can compute the entropy following the Shannon definition or the average $\pT$ as the Bjorken-type energy estimator. Additionally, we estimate the temperature from the slope of the $\pT$ spectrum at low $\pT$ values. We use the Hagedorn and Tricomi functions to describe the $\pT$ spectrum within a nonextensive approach and determine consistent thermodynamic frameworks by solving the fundamental relation $dE/dT=C$, where $C=TdS/dT$ is the heat capacity. We found that the internal energy behaves nonlinearly at LHC energies, indicating that the count of degrees of freedom is more complex than simply adding the number of flavors present in the hadron production. The main implication of our results is that the systems produced in pp collisions depart from the ideal gas picture and explain why the production of high $\pT$ hadrons has always been observed, even in earlier experiments, which may also encompass other experiments colliding e$^-$p or e$^+$e$^-$.

item.title: Performance Evaluation of Straw Tubes with Muon Beams at CERN
item.description: arXiv:2604.16245v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present results from two test beam campaigns that investigate the performance of straw tube detectors as potential candidates for an FCC-ee straw tracker. These studies were carried out at CERN using 150 GeV muon beams. Dedicated algorithms were developed to determine both single tube spatial resolution for the primary coordinate in the $r-\phi$ plane and spatial resolution for the secondary coordinate along the tube direction within a straw chamber. Detection efficiency was also evaluated as a function of the extrapolated hit position for each tube. Both datasets showed consistent results for spatial resolutions and efficiency. The average single-tube spatial resolution in the primary $r-\phi$ coordinate is approximately 110 $\mu$m, while the average spatial resolution in the secondary coordinate along the tube direction is approximately 2 mm. Most tubes show a single-tube detection efficiency above 98%.

item.title: $CP$ violation in neutral kaon mixing in $D^0\rightarrow K_SK_S$
item.description: arXiv:2605.00989v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study CP violation induced by neutral kaon mixing in $a_{CP}(D^0 \rightarrow K_S K_S)$. We show that the contribution from neutral kaon mixing arises only in connection with second-order weak interactions in $D$ decays. We estimate this effect to be at the $10^{-6}$ level, and thus negligible compared to current experimental sensitivity and to the expected contribution from CP violation in the charm sector. Similar reasoning can be applied to other systems.
item.dc:creator: Yuval Grossman, Guglielmo Papiri, Stefan Schacht

item.title: Search for charged long-lived particles at the Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee)
item.description: arXiv:2605.23793v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Long-lived particles (LLPs) have emerged as a compelling signature of physics beyond the standard model, offering unique discovery opportunities at current and future colliders. We present an analysis of charged LLPs leading to signatures with kinked tracks and displaced vertices. Using timing information the search is extended to detector-stable LLPs. We explore the discovery prospects of such particles at the Future Circular Collider~(FCC-ee), a proposed $e^{+}e^{-}$ collider. The clean collision environment of FCC-ee and excellent tracking performance of the IDEA detector enhance the sensitivity to kinked-track signatures, which are considerably more challenging to reconstruct in the high-occupancy environment of hadron colliders. The excellent timing resolution of the timing layer enables us to infer the mass of the detector stable particles. As a benchmark the stau pair production in the gauge mediated supersymmetry breaking (GMSB) within the minimal supersymmetric standard model scenario is considered. In this model the lightest supersymmetric particle is a gravitino and the next-to-lightest supersymmetric particle is the stau, the superpartner of the tau lepton. Discovery sensitivity up to the kinematic limit is obtained for the $ZH$ and $t\bar{t}$ runs of the planned FCC-ee operation. We demonstrate that a potential discovery would allow for a precise $\tilde\tau$ mass measurement.
item.dc:creator: Soumyaa Vashishtha, Mirindra Randriamanantena, Thomas Creuset, Maximilian Goblirsch-Kolb, Isabell Melzer-Pellmann

item.title: Full Characterization of a Mock Nuclear Waste Barrel with Muon Tomography using Micromegas Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2606.02557v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Muon tomography based on multiple Coulomb scattering provides a non-destructive method to image dense and shielded objects using naturally occurring cosmic-ray muons. In the context of nuclear waste characterization, we present the experimental imaging of a 205-L mock waste barrel using a dedicated 1m$^2$ muon scattering tomography test bench. The system employs multiplexed resistive Micromegas detectors, enabling stable and high-precision muon tracking. Monte Carlo simulations are first used to characterize material-dependent scattering signatures and to quantitatively assess identification performance using statistical reconstruction. These simulation-based results are then used to define objective discrimination thresholds, which are subsequently applied to experimental data for the localization and identification of internal anomalies. Using an Angle Statistics Reconstruction algorithm, we achieve a spatial resolution of 10 mm and demonstrate the three-dimensional imaging of an internal structure containing both low- and high-radiation length materials. Material discrimination performance is evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, yielding high identification efficiency for dense metallic inclusions such as lead and steel (AUC $\geq$ 0.96) within acquisition times of a few days, while cavities also exhibit strong contrast. Experimental results show good agreement with detailed Monte Carlo simulations. By establishing a continuous workflow from simulation-based performance characterization to practical application on measured data, this work provides a quantitatively validated framework for muon scattering tomography applied to complex, shielded objects.
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el Bajou, David Atti\'e, H\'ector G\'omez, Irakli Mandjavidze, Philippe Mas

item.title: Mass spectra and electromagnetic characteristics of the $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ and $K^{(*)}{D}^{(*)}$ molecular tetraquarks from the coupled-channel dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2606.13088v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by the observation of numerous charmed-strange hadrons lying close to the $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ and $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ thresholds, we systematically investigate their mass spectra and electromagnetic characteristics, explicitly incorporating the $S$-$D$ wave mixing and coupled-channel effects. For the mass spectra, we employ the one-boson-exchange model and obtain several promising $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ and $K^{(*)}D^{(*)}$ molecular candidates awaiting future experimental confirmation. The coupled-channel dynamics is found to play an essential role: it not only enhances binding in existing channels but also generates new loosely bound states that are absent in the single-channel approximation. Regarding the electromagnetic characteristics, we discuss the M1 radiative decay widths and magnetic moments of these charmed-strange molecular tetraquarks based on our obtained mass spectra and spatial wave functions within the constituent quark model. Our results demonstrate that the electromagnetic observables serve as valuable discriminants for clarifying the nature of these hadronic molecules. We encourage experimental collaborations to focus on such predicted charmed-strange molecular tetraquark candidates, especially the genuinely exotic $K^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)}$ states comprising four different flavors with valence quark content $\bar c \bar s u d$.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Ning Cui, Fu-Lai Wang

item.title: Unitarity limits on HH production from VBF mediated channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.07194v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we study the unitarity constraints on double Higgs production from Vector Boson Fusion mediated channels, specifically in $f_1 f_2 \to f_3 f_4 H_5 H_6$ scattering, where $f$ refers generically to either fermion or anti-fermion, and both cases with quarks and leptons will be considered. We focus on the beyond Standard Model contributions from anomalous quartic couplings of two electroweak gauge bosons and two Higgs bosons ($VVHH$ with $VV=WW, ZZ$) from effective operators containing four derivatives. These four derivative operators appear in the two most popular effective field theories, SMEFT (at canonical dimension 8) and HEFT (at chiral dimension 4), and their corresponding $VVHH$ effective vertices can be easily related for the considered processes here. The aim of this work is to derive jointly the unitarity constraints on these related effective vertices using the peculiarities of the VBF mediated channels with four particles in the final state while keeping the propagation of the internal $VV$ pairs being off-shell as it must be for these channels. We also discuss the relevance of the obtained constraints for $f_1 f_2 \to f_3 f_4 H_5 H_6$ at high energy colliders.
item.dc:creator: A. Dobado, D. Domenech, M. Herrero, R. A. Morales
